notes:
Notes for the question "Who is the greatest football player in history?" (as of Oct 12, 2026). The question is a matter of opinion, so the search found no single official answer.

**Consensus in 2026 rankings**
- Daily Sabah's ranking of the 50 greatest, from about 65 days ago, puts Lionel Messi first. It says he is ahead of Pelé, Diego Maradona and Cristiano Ronaldo in most modern evaluations. It cites his 2022 World Cup win, record eight Ballon d'Or awards and longevity. It also names Cruyff, Beckenbauer, Ronaldo Nazário, Zidane and Di Stéfano in the next tier.
- Sportda's 2026 top-50 ranking, from about 52 days ago, also has Messi at No. 1. It has Pelé at No. 3 and Cristiano Ronaldo at No. 7.
- Footballberry's 2026 top-10 list, from about 128 days ago, has Messi first, Pelé second and Ronaldo fourth.
- FourFourTwo's top-100 list, from about 98 days ago, has Pelé at No. 3 and Cristiano Ronaldo at No. 5. The page I saw did not show its No. 1 or No. 2.
- The PFSA says most pundits name either Ronaldo or Messi. It calls Messi "debatedly" the best of all time.
- Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said after the 2026 World Cup final that Messi is the best football player ever to step on a pitch (ESPN).
- Not every list agrees. One list (givemesport.com) names Pelé among its top few, and the search did not show who it ranks first.

**Facts the rankings cite**
- Messi has eight Ballon d'Or awards; no other player has won more than five (Sportda). He scored 672 official goals for Barcelona (Sportda).
- Pelé is the only man to win three World Cups (Sportda, Footballberry).
- Ronaldo is the all-time leading scorer in men's international football and in Champions League history, and has five Ballon d'Or awards (Sportda). He scored at the 2026 World Cup at age 41, the only man to score at five World Cups (Sportda).
- PFSA says Ronaldo is approaching 970 career goals and chasing 1,000.

**Recent events**
- Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 World Cup final on July 19, 2026. Ferran Torres scored the winner (NBC, ESPN). Messi, 39, was on the losing side and had 8 goals and 4 assists in the tournament (ESPN).
- ESPN reports Mbappé won the Golden Boot ahead of Messi, and Rodri won the Golden Ball.
- NBC New York noted that a win would have further cemented Messi's legacy as the greatest of all time. Messi had said this was his last World Cup, and his international future is unclear (ESPN).

**Gaps and caveats**
- Sources disagree on the order. Most put Messi first, with Pelé, Maradona and Ronaldo next, but the order differs by list.
- Several of these are low-authority listicle sites, and none is an official or statistical ranking.
- The results did not say whether Messi's 2026 World Cup changed any major list's order.
